answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to collateral held outside itself: a newcomer locks a ferrous stake of real value in an unrelated economy, bonded to a crystal-clear public record linking the two accounts, with the pigment of its history — past transactions, counterparties, age — graded before admission. Each extra fake demands a fresh external stake with its own history, so a farm's cost multiplies with every head, and detection here slashes the stake there, where the farm cannot print replacements.
